optionalfeature.name: Backstep Shot
entries: When you switch to a ranged weapon, you can immediately move 5 feet without provoking any {@action Opportunity Attack|PHB|attacks of opportunity}.

optionalfeature.name: Cannon Throw
entries: When you to switch to a melee weapon with the {@itemProperty T|PHB|Thrown} property, you can give yourself {@quickref Advantage and Disadvantage|PHB|2|0|advantage} on your attack roll when throwing that weapon using Strength.

optionalfeature.name: Close the Gap
entries: When you to switch to a {@itemProperty L|PHB|Light} weapon, you can immediately move 5 feet towards a creature before you attack it. If the attack hits, you add a {@damage 1d4} die to the attack's damage roll.

optionalfeature.name: Defensive Slash
entries: When you switch to a melee weapon with the {@itemProperty F|PHB|Finesse} property, you can use your bonus action to take on a defensive stance. Your AC is increased by {@dice 1d4} until the beginning of your next turn. The effect ends early if you take damage.

optionalfeature.name: Extended Strike
entries: When you switch to a {@itemProperty V|PHB|Versatile} weapon and use it with one hand, you can give that weapon the {@itemProperty R|PHB|Reach} property for your attack.

optionalfeature.name: Fast Sweep
entries: When you switch to a melee weapon with the {@itemProperty R|PHB|Reach} property, you can make your attack with this weapon a {@action Shove|PHB} action instead. This {@action Shove|PHB} action has the reach of the melee weapon.

optionalfeature.name: Momentum Strike
entries: When you switch to a {@itemProperty H|PHB|Heavy} melee weapon, you can make that weapon gain the {@itemProperty F|PHB|Finesse} property for your attack.

optionalfeature.name: Overhead Strike
entries: When you switch to a {@itemProperty 2H|PHB|Two-Handed} melee weapon and your attack hits, the target has {@quickref Advantage and Disadvantage|PHB|2|0|disadvantage} on its Constitution saving throw to maintain {@status concentration}.

optionalfeature.name: Point-Blank Shot
entries: When you switch to a {@itemProperty H|phb|Heavy} ranged weapon and your attack hits a target within 5 feet range, you can use your bonus action to follow up with a bash that knocks the target {@condition prone} if it is Large or smaller.

optionalfeature.name: Shield Bash
entries: When you wield a {@item shield|phb}, you can make a melee weapon attack with your {@item shield|phb}. The attack uses a {@damage d4} as its damage die. If the attack hits, the creature has {@quickref Advantage and Disadvantage|PHB|2|0|disadvantage} on its next attack roll.

optionalfeature.name: Strikethrough
entries: When you switch to a {@itemProperty V|PHB|Versatile} weapon and use it with two hands, you can add {@dice 1d4} to the attack roll with this weapon.

optionalfeature.name: Surprise Attack
entries: When you switch to an {@quickref Improvised Weapons||1||improvised weapon}, you can attempt to create an opening. If the attack hits, the next melee weapon attack against this target has {@quickref Advantage and Disadvantage|PHB|2|0|advantage}.

optionalfeature.name: Thrashing Attack
entries: When you switch to a {@item mace|PHB}, {@item flail|PHB}, {@item morningstar|PHB} or {@item war pick|PHB}, you can add {@dice 1d4} to the attack roll with this weapon. If the target is wielding a {@item shield|PHB} you may add another {@dice 1d4} to the attack roll.

subclassFeature.name: Combat Sage
entries: Fighters have practiced combat using all kinds of weaponry, but only a Combat Sage knows how to gain a significant advantage based on the basic training. Through dedication, creativity and fast moves a Combat Sage is able to use weapons beyond their intended purposes.

subclassFeature.name: Muscle Memory
entries: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, your training has conditioned your muscles to move fast and with precision, allowing you to arm yourself and switch weapons without thinking about it.

As part of a weapon attack you can drop or sheathe your weapons, which you are currently wielding, or change your grip on a {@itemProperty V|PHB|versatile} weapon before you attack. As part of the same motion you can then pick up or draw different weapons to attack with. You can also don or doff a {@item shield|phb} as if it were a weapon.
This feature does not use up your free action to interact with an object (except for weapons and shields).

subclassFeature.name: Relentless Practice
entries: At 3rd level, you learn weapon arts that allow you to wield weapons with certain properties more efficiently. When using {@subclassFeature Muscle Memory|Fighter||Combat Sage|CombatSage|3} to switch to a weapon of different type than you were wielding before or to change your grip on a {@itemProperty V|PHB|versatile} weapon, you may use a weapon art as part of your attack with that weapon.
You may use only one weapon art during an attack action, regardless of the number of attacks during this action. Starting at 10th level you can use two weapon arts during an attack action.

entries.name: Weapon Arts
entries: You learn three weapon arts of your choice, which are detailed under "Weapon Arts" below. A list of the available options can also be found on the {@filter Optional Features|optionalfeatures|feature type=wa:cs} page. You learn three additional weapon arts at 7th and 15th level. Each time you learn new weapon arts you can replace one weapon art you know with a different one.

subclassFeature.name: Warfare Study
entries: Starting at 7th level, you have studied the art of war and it's tools extensively and you understand how warriors and generals think. You gain advantage on Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}, {@skill History}) and Wisdom ({@skill Nature}, {@skill Insight}) checks with respect to weaponry, combat and warfare.

subclassFeature.name: Additional Weapon Arts
entries: You learn three additional weapon arts of your choice, which are detailed under "Weapon Arts" here and above. A list of the available options can also be found on the {@filter Optional Features|optionalfeatures|feature type=wa:cs} page. You learn three additional weapon arts at 15th level. Each time you learn new weapon arts you can replace one weapon art you know with a different one.

subclassFeature.name: Turn the Tide
entries: At 10th level, you have learned to anticipate enemy attacks and occasionally use the most dangerous ones to your advantage. When an enemy melee weapon hits you, you may use your reaction to take the {@action Disarm|dmg} action on the enemy's weapon before the attack deals damage. If you fail, you are vulnerable to the damage of the attack. If you succeed, you may immediately use {@subclassFeature Muscle Memory|Fighter||Combat Sage|CombatSage|3} to wield that weapon and attack that creature. If your attack hits, it is automatically considered a critical hit.
Once you have used this ability successfully against a creature, you cannot use it against it again.

subclassFeature.name: Swift Precision
entries: At 15th level, you have practiced the art of wielding different weapons with speed and precision. When using {@subclassFeature Muscle Memory|Fighter||Combat Sage|CombatSage|3} to switch weapons you may add {@damage 1d4} to your next attack roll.

subclassFeature.name: Additional Weapon Arts
entries: You learn three additional weapon arts of your choice, which are detailed under "Weapon Arts" here and above. A list of the available options can also be found on the {@filter Optional Features|optionalfeatures|feature type=wa:cs} page. Each time you learn new weapon arts you can replace one weapon art you know with a different one.

subclassFeature.name: Dismember
entries: At 18th level, you have learned to fight soldiers and monsters alike. When fighting a creature that cannot be {@action disarm|dmg|disarmed} you can attempt to cut off part of its body instead of {@action disarm|dmg|disarming} it. You make an attack roll contested by the target's Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check or Constitution saving throw. If you win the contest, the creature loses a part of its body (such as a claw, horn or arm - determined by the DM) and your attack deals damage and is automatically considered a critical hit.
You may treat the cut-off body part as an improvised weapon that uses a {@dice d12} as its damage die and deals bludgeoning damage (unless otherwise specified by the DM).
Once you have used this ability successfully against a creature, you cannot use it against it again.
